The following set of functions help to pre-process and organize audio and corresponding metadata. In conjunction, these tools allow you to select recordings parameterized to a specific study design.

```{r include = FALSE, echo = F, warning = F, message = F}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = '#>'
)

library(wildrtrax)
library(dplyr)

```

## Scanning audio files from a directory

The `wt_audio_scanner()` function reads in audio files (either wac, wav or flac format) from a local directory and outputs useful metadata.

```{r echo=TRUE, include=TRUE, eval=F, warning = F, message = F}
wt_audio_scanner(path = ".", file_type = "wav", extra_cols = T)

```

You might want to select recordings between certain times of day or year, or filter recordings based on some criteria.

```{r echo=TRUE, include=TRUE, eval=F, warning = F, message = F}
files |>
  dplyr::select(-file_path)

```

```{r echo=TRUE, include=TRUE, eval=F, warning = F, message = F}
files |>
  dplyr::mutate(hour = as.numeric(format(recording_date_time, "%H"))) |>
  dplyr::filter(julian == 176, 
         hour %in% c(4:8))

```

## Running the QUT Ecoacoustics AnalysisPrograms software on a wt_* standard data set

The `wt_run_ap()` function allows you to run the QUT Analysis Programs [(AP.exe)](https://ap.qut.ecoacoustics.info/) on your audio data. AP generates acoustic index values and false-colour spectrograms for each audio minute of data. Note that you must have the AP program installed on your computer. See more with @towsey2018.

```{r echo=TRUE, include=T, eval=F, warning = F, message = F}
# Use the wt_* tibble to execute the AP on the files

wt_run_ap(x = my_files, output_dir = paste0(root, 'ap_outputs'), path_to_ap = '/where/you/store/AP')

```

Then use `wt_glean_ap()` to plot the acoustic index and long-duration false-colour spectrogram (LDFC) results.

```{r echo=T, include=T, eval=F, warning=F, message, prompt=T, comment=""}
# This example is from ABMI's Ecosystem Health Monitoring program

my_files <- wt_audio_scanner(".../ABMI-986-SE", file_type = "wav", extra_cols = )

wt_glean_ap(my_files |>
               dplyr::mutate(hour = as.numeric(format(recording_date_time, "%H"))) |>
               filter(between(julian,110,220),
                      hour %in% c(0:3,22:23)), input_dir = ".../ap_outputs", purpose = "biotic")

```

![Indices of all recordings from julian date 110-220 and from 22h00-03h00](986-se-indices.png)

![Long-duration false-colour spectrogram (LDFC) of all recordings from julian date 110-220 and from 22h00-03h00](986-se.png)

## Applying a limited amplitude filter

We can use the `wt_signal_level()` function to search for sounds that exceed a certain amplitude threshold. 

```{r, echo=T, include=TRUE, eval=F, warning=F, message=F}
if (dir.exists(".")) {
  signal_file <- wt_audio_scanner(path = ".", file_type = "wav", extra_cols = T)
} else {
  'Can\'\t find this directory'
}

wt_signal_level(path = signal_file$file_path, 
                     fmin = 0, 
                     fmax = 10000, 
                     threshold = 5, 
                     channel = 'left')

```

```{r, eval = F}
# Run
s
# Return a list object, with parameters stored
str(s)

# We can view the output:
s['output']
# We have eleven detections that exceeded this threshold.

```

# Linking data to WildTrax

`wt_make_aru_tasks()` generates tasks from any `wt_*` standard data set. The only columns it needs are `location`, `recording_date_time`, `recording_sample_frequency` and `recording_duration`. Any extra columns are ignored, so you don't need to trim your data first. There are two common ways to get there.

## Generate tasks from recordings already in WildTrax

Use this when the media is already uploaded and you want tasks for a subset of it, for example recordings where a classifier detected a species of interest.

Start by pulling your organization's recordings with `wt_get_sync(api = "organization_recordings")` or `wt_get_view("organization_recordings")` if you want additional columns (see `vignette("apis", package = "wildrtrax")`. The `ai_threshold` argument sets the minimum classifier confidence used for the detection columns at 0.5 but can be changed as needed. Depending on how many recordings your organization has, this can take a moment as it iterates through the pages of recordings available.

```{r eval=F, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=T}
recs <- wt_get_view("organization_recordings", organization = 5466, ai_threshold = 0.9)
```

The result has one row per recording, including location, date and time, weather and astronomical variables, and the species detected by each classifier (`birdnet_common_name`, `hawkears_common_name`). Filter it down to the recordings you want to listen to:

```{r eval=F, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=T}
alfl_recs <- recs |>
  dplyr::filter(hawkears_common_name == "Alder Flycatcher")
```

You can filter on any column, such as dates, locations, time of day or weather, or combine several conditions:

```{r eval=F, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=T}
alfl_recs <- recs |>
  dplyr::filter(
    hawkears_common_name == "Alder Flycatcher",
    recording_month %in% 5:7,
    weather == "Clear/Sunny"
  )
```

Then pass the filtered data to `wt_make_aru_tasks()`, choosing a task method and a task length in seconds:

```{r eval=F, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=T}
alfl_tasks <- alfl_recs |>
  wt_make_aru_tasks(task_method = "1SPT", task_length = 60)
```

## Generate tasks from media on your computer

Use this when you have recordings that you haven't processed or uploaded yet.

Scan your media with `wt_audio_scanner()` and a folder path:

```{r eval=F, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=T}
my_files <- wt_audio_scanner(path = "/my/BigGrid/files", file_type = "all", extra_cols = F)
```

Next, find out what WildTrax already has. Download the recordings for your organization and compare them to your files on `location` and `recording_date_time`. An `anti_join()` leaves only the media that hasn't been uploaded yet:

```{r eval=F, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=T}
recs <- wt_get_sync("organization_recordings", organization = 5466)

to_upload <- my_files |>
  dplyr::anti_join(recs, by = c("location", "recording_date_time"))
```

Alternatively, if you only want to compare against particular projects, download their main reports:

```{r eval=F, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=T}
my_projects <- wt_get_projects("ARU") |>
  dplyr::filter(grepl("Cypress", project)) |>
  dplyr::pull(project_id) |>
  wt_download_report(sensor_id = "ARU", reports = "main")
```

Once you have the list of media to process, generate the tasks:

```{r eval=F, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=T}
new_tasks <- to_upload |>
  dplyr::select(-file_path) |>
  wt_make_aru_tasks(task_method = "1SPT", task_length = 180)
```

## Integrating legacy data from classifiers

The `wildrtrax` package provides tools for integrating classifier outputs from Wildlife Acoustics’ [Kaleidoscope](https://www.wildlifeacoustics.com/products/kaleidoscope-pro) and [Songscope](https://answers.wildlifeacoustics.com/) into WildTrax-compatible data formats using the `wt_songscope_tags()` and `wt_kaleidoscope_tags()` functions. These functions convert classifier-generated detections into WildTrax tags, allowing each detection to be uploaded as an individual task-associated tag. This supports workflows where audio data have already been processed by external classifiers, enabling existing detections to be reformatted, aligned with media, and uploaded to WildTrax for further review and analysis.

```{r include = FALSE, eval = T}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)

Sys.setenv(WT_USERNAME = "guest", WT_PASSWORD = "Apple123")

```

Here is some raw Songscope output:

```{r eval=T, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=T}
# Convert Songscope output into WildTrax tags

readr::read_table("./CONI.txt")

```

And here's in the transformation with `wt_songscope_tags()`:

```{r eval=F, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=T}
wt_songscope_tags(
  input = "./CONI.txt",
  output = "env",
  output_file = NULL,
  species = "CONI",
  vocalization = "SONG",
  score_filter = 10,
  method = "1SPT",
  duration = 180,
  sample_freq = 44100
)

```

Similarly, a Kaleidoscope output can be converted similarly:

```{r eval=F, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=T}
wt_kaleidoscope_tags(
  input = "./id.csv",
  output = NULL,
  freq_bump = T) # Add a 20000 Hz frequency buffer to the tag

```
